properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be

* WHERE...Portions of central, eastern, and western New Mexico.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

merging storm systems will bring a prolonged multi-day period of

potentially reaching flood stage. Recent burn scars may see flash
flooding, including the Ruidoso area burn scars, Frijoles,
Sacaton, Hummingbird, and Whiskey burn scars.

properties.areaDesc: Fisher; Nolan; Sterling; Coke; Runnels; Irion; Tom Green; Concho; Crockett; Schleicher; Sutton; Haskell; Throckmorton; Jones; Shackelford; Taylor; Callahan; Coleman; Brown; McCulloch; San Saba; Menard; Kimble; Mason
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 1:18AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Nolan,
Runnels, San Saba, Schleicher, Shackelford, Sterling, Sutton,
Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding is possible.

- Multiple rounds of heavy rain are possible through Thursday night
as an influx of moisture arrives from the remnants of a tropical
disturbance. This will coincide with an approaching upper level
low pressure system and an associated frontal boundary. High
precipitable water values will support efficient rainfall
production with this activity. Model guidance suggests heavy rain
and thunderstorms capable of producing rainfall totals in the 2
to 4 inch range across the watch area. Locally higher amounts of
7+ inches can occur.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 28 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Snowfall beginning Monday night could potentially lead to slick
travel conditions in Isabel Pass beginning Monday night. Cooler
temperatures are expected to settle in through midweek which
could allow for 3" to 6" of snow through Wednesday morning.
Another round of snow is likely Wednesday evening into Thursday
morning. This could be the start of the permanent snow pack.

NWSheadline: Moderate to Heavy Snowfall Expected Across the Eastern Alaska Range

properties.areaDesc: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Fortymile Country; Upper Chena River Valley; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 28 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Light rain and snow will meander around the Interior. Locations
above 2000ft have the highest chance for snow through Monday
night but snow levels continue to drop to 1000ft Tuesday. Valley
locations, including Fairbanks, may see some snowflakes mix in
with rain beginning Tuesday night with flurries lingering into
Wednesday. Little to no accumulation is expected in the valleys
through Wednesday afternoon. Between 1000-2000ft, up to 1 inch of
snow is possible but there will be melting as the snow reaches the
ground. Above 2000ft, 1 to 3 inches of snow is possible through
Wednesday afternoon. Another round of light snow is becoming more
likely Wednesday night into Thursday with minor accumulations
possible, even in Fairbanks.

NWSheadline: First Round of Snowfall Across Portions of the Interior

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 28 at 1:28PM PDT until September 30 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves of 3 to 5
feet. Minor tidal overflows possible, especially Monday and
Tuesday.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas (including Santa Barbara Harbor).
Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant damage
is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Locally moderate coastal flooding impacts
possible but unlikely for areas such as Santa Barbara Harbor.
These impacts may include moderate flooding of sea water over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Additionally, locally moderate
beach erosion is possible.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
